R0173.title: Gas Fee Manipulation
R0173.definition: Attackers manipulate blockchain transaction gas fees to affect transaction order or cause network congestion.
R0173.description: Gas fees determine transaction priority in blocks. Attackers can: set extremely high gas fees for front-running, send large amounts of low-gas transactions to clog the network, exploit gas price volatility for arbitrage, manipulate gas auction mechanisms, etc., causing ordinary user transactions to delay or fail, or forcing users to pay higher fees.
R0173.influence: User transaction costs skyrocket, network congestion paralysis, transaction order maliciously manipulated.

observables: Transactions with gas fees far above normal levels appear within a block, ordered immediately following victim transactions
Network gas prices are anomalously driven up within a short window by large volumes of low-gas transactions or high-gas bidding
The same sender repeatedly executes arbitrage with extremely high gas fees to front-run transactions across multiple transactions
The pending transaction pool is filled with large volumes of low-gas transactions, causing normal transactions to be delayed for extended periods

R0173-001.title: Gas Fee Manipulation and Frontrunning
R0173-001.definition: Miners or validators exploit transaction ordering rights to front-run user transactions through gas fee bidding or collude with arbitrage bots to extract MEV profits.

references.title: Flash Boys 2.0: Frontrunning in Decentralized Exchanges
Ethereum is a Dark Forest - MEV Threats

R0173-001.description:
Gas fee manipulation and frontrunning exploit transaction ordering, fee bidding, and block construction. Attackers insert transactions before or after user actions for arbitrage or disruption, including sandwich attacks, liquidation sniping, NFT mint frontrunning, and malicious fee escalation.

The risk increases user slippage, trading cost, and perceived unfairness. DeFi protocols need private order flow, slippage controls, batch auctions, and MEV mitigation patterns.
R0173-001.influence: Frontrunning and gas manipulation increase slippage and trading costs, distort DeFi markets, and weaken confidence in transaction fairness.

observables: A user-submitted DeFi transaction is front-run by an arbitrage bot transaction before packaging, forming a sandwich attack
Block builders collude with arbitrage bots to prioritize specific transactions to extract MEV profits
In NFT mint or liquidation scenarios, user transactions are front-run at high frequency, resulting in failures or unfavorable execution prices
The actual execution price of a user transaction shows slippage beyond a reasonable range compared to the expected price at submission
